text:
ash: FYI ran into a reconciliation surprise in prod: model provenance returned two session owners and our current claim flow merged them under the first tenant. downstream finance asked for a clear auditable chain for any late attributions

dina: do we have sample event? curious whether this is a provenance merge vs enrichment overwrite

ash: pasted minimal shape: proxy attaches request_fingerprint=sha1(...), enrichment added tenant_hint=[T1], runtime provenance returned owners=[T1,T2] and cost_breakdown tokens=420. final claim only referenced T1

omar: low-effort option is to attach an owners[] field to claim and let billing UI decide split. downside: ledger becomes multi-owner which complicates chargeback and kudu reports

rachel: alternative: keep ledger single-owner but emit sidecar "adjustment" events for secondary owners. ledger stays append-only per invoice line, and adjustments are separate, signed, and link back to original_claim_id

ash: sidecars sound appealing for audit trail. question: how to dedupe if adjustment job retries or if original claim is reingested?
omar: use a deterministic adjustment_key: sha256(versioned_fingerprint|adjustment_type|target_owner). versioned_fingerprint = sha1(payload_v2) so changes to enrichment logic produce different keys. On emit we check a durable dedupe set (bigtable/redis) and only write once
dina: bigtable TTL for dedupe keys? we need retention at least 90 days to cover invoice disputes. storing everything forever costly

omar: dedupe entries can be TTLed after 90d, but adjustments themselves go into the ledger/audit store with full retention. dedupe set is just for preventing duplicates during replay windows

rachel: operationally, we should also expose an adjustments_by_delay metric and a per-tenant late_adjustment_count. If a tenant gets > X late_adjustments/day, trigger an ops alert and notify their account owner

ash: how do we decide split semantics? equal split vs marker-based? some customers want deterministic primary-owner wins policy to avoid surprises

omar: propose configurable tenant-level policy: default=primary-owner-wins, opt-in=proportional. proportional requires richer signals from runtime (per-turn token attribution or marker spans). we can surface an opt-in flag via billing API and console

rachel: agree. default simple behavior reduces blast radius. add a migration plan: existing tenants implicitly primary-owner; new tenants can request proportional via support flow while we add self-serve toggle

ash: ledger schema changes? we need to add columns: adjustment_origin (string), adjustment_key (string), original_claim_id (string), split_policy (string). Keep them nullable so backfill is cheap

omar: small SQL example for creating adjustment rows:

```
INSERT INTO billing.claims (claim_id, tenant_id, tokens, amount_cents, original_claim_id, adjustment_origin, adjustment_key, created_at)
VALUES (uuid_generate_v4(), $tenant, $tokens, $amt, $orig_id, 'stitcher_v1', $dedupe_key, now())
```

ash: tests: 1) replay original claim then run stitcher twice -> only one adjustment. 2) original claim reprocessed after adjustment -> should not double deduct

rachel: also need to update invoice rendering: show original line, then adjustments grouped by invoice period with a delta and link to provenance. UI should display original_event_fingerprint and stitch_run_id

billing-bot: Scheduled job "stitcher-reconcile" created. next run: 2024-09-01T02:00:00Z.

dina: performance concern: if we propagate owners[] early across all paths we add ~200 bytes per request. at 10k qps that's significant. prefer stitcher async unless we can compress envelope (hashes only)

omar: compromise: proxy embeds owner_hints_hash and request_fingerprint only; runtime may return full owners list to stitcher which does heavy lifting off the hot path

ash: agreed. action items: 1) adopt adjustment sidecar model and ledger nullable fields (omar) 2) implement deterministic dedupe_key (omar/dina) 3) default policy primary-owner-wins, add opt-in proportional flag (rachel) 4) metrics + alerts + UI links for adjustments (dina/rachel) 5) test plan for replay/dedup (ash/omar)

rachel: i'll draft a short RFC with concrete schema changes and example invoice UI snippets, ping @finance and @support for opt-in workflow

ash: thanks team. i'll add a short section in the incident playbook about how to handle disputes from late adjustments

sysops: Note: created temporary dashboard "billing:late-adjustments" with panels for delay histogram and top-20 affected tenants.

omar: will pair with ash on integration tests tomorrow. I'll post a prototype dedupe lib link in this thread once ready

ash: perfect — closing out here, RFC link once drafted.
